question: In which year was the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) established? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: 1982
1992
1947
1977
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1982

Explanation:
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established on July 12, 1982. It was formed on the recommendations of the Shivaraman Committee to provide financial assistance for agriculture and rural development. NABARD's headquarters is located in Mumbai. Its primary objective is to provide credit for agriculture, small-scale industries, and rural development. NABARD also plays a crucial role in developing rural infrastructure through schemes like the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF). It was set up by the Government of India in collaboration with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

☛ Which committee recommended the formation of NABARD? → Shivaraman Committee
☛ When was NABARD established? → July 12, 1982
☛ Which fund managed by NABARD for rural infrastructure? → RIDF (Rural Infrastructure Development Fund)
☛ What is the apex financial institution for agriculture and rural development? → NABARD

question: Recently, Indian Defence Minister attended the Victory Day Parade in Moscow, Russia on the occasion of the 75th anniversary of the Soviet victory over ____. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Germany

question: Who was the founding director of BARC Mumbai? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Homi Jehangir Bhabha
Vikram Sarabhai
Satish Dhawan
Raja Ramanna
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Homi Jehangir Bhabha

Explanation:
Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha, widely regarded as the father of the Indian nuclear program, founded the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) in Mumbai in 1954 and served as its first director. He also established the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and the Atomic Energy Commission of India. A brilliant physicist, he shaped India's nuclear energy policy. Under his leadership, India's first nuclear reactor, APSARA, achieved criticality. BARC remains India's premier nuclear research facility.

☛ Who was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission of India? → Homi J. Bhabha

question: Which of the following countries is the largest producer of gold in the world in 2019? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: South Africa
China
India
Australia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is China

Explanation:
In 2019, China was the world's largest producer of gold. Since 2007, China has maintained this position, surpassing South Africa. China's annual gold production has been around 380-400 tonnes. It is followed by Australia and Russia. India is a major consumer of gold but not a top producer. South Africa, once the largest producer, has seen a decline in output and is no longer in the top three. Thus, China is the correct answer as the leading gold producer in 2019.

question: Which of the following countries is not a member of the World Bank Group? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Canada
China
Cuba
USA
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cuba

Explanation:
The World Bank Group consists of 189 member countries. Cuba is not a member of the World Bank Group. Cuba withdrew its membership from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund in 1960. In contrast, Canada, China, and the USA are members of the World Bank Group. The World Bank Group includes five institutions: the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association, the International Finance Corporation, the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes. Despite being a member of the United Nations, Cuba is not part of the World Bank Group.

question: The 21st commonwealth games were held in: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: Who among the following never became United Nation’s Secretary General? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Kofi Annan
Ban Ki-moon
Dag Hammarskjold
Louise Frechette
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Louise Frechette

Explanation:
Louise Frechette was a Canadian diplomat who served as the Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations, but she never became the Secretary-General. Kofi Annan (Ghana) served from 1997-2006, Ban Ki-moon (South Korea) from 2007-2016, and Dag Hammarskjöld (Sweden) from 1953-1961. Hammarskjöld died in a plane crash in 1961 while in office. The UN Secretary-General is the chief administrative officer, appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council. So far, Secretaries-General have come from Asia, Africa, Europe, and Latin America, but Frechette was never one of them.

question: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) is a historic document that was adopted by the United Nations on: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)

31 December 1945

Explanation:
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1948 in Paris. It is a landmark document that for the first time set out fundamental human rights to be universally protected. The UDHR consists of 30 articles covering civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights. It was drafted by a committee chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt. question: In which year was the International Labour Organisation (ILO) established? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: 1931
1919
1921
1909
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1919

Explanation:
The International Labour Organisation (ILO) was established in 1919 as part of the Treaty of Versailles. It was originally an agency of the League of Nations and later became a specialized agency of the United Nations in 1946. The ILO's primary goals include promoting workers' rights, enhancing employment opportunities, and fostering social justice. Its headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland. The ILO is known for its tripartite structure, where governments, employers, and worker representatives participate equally. It was the first international organization to set labor standards and has influenced labor laws worldwide. The ILO received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969 for its efforts to improve peace and social justice.
